back: Bit by bit: 1100 and 1010. `&` keeps bits set in both (1000), `|` keeps bits set in either (1110), `^` keeps bits set in exactly one (0110).

front: What does `~x` give for an integer `x`?
back: `~` flips every bit, which works out to `-x - 1`. That is why `~5` is `-6`, not a smaller positive number.
`<<` shifts bits left, multiplying by 2 for each step. `>>` shifts right, dividing by 2 each step and dropping the remainder.

front: What does this print? Compare `&` with `and`.
back: Shifts bind looser than `+`, so it is `(1 + 2) << 1`. `&` works on bits (110 and 011 gives 2), while `and` is Boolean and returns its second operand `3` when both are truthy.
